newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Cintra 1996 net 625.24 mln pesos.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Cintra 1996 net 625.24 mln pesos.

text.p: Mexican airline company Cintra SA on Wednesday reported 1996 net profits of 625.24 million pesos, according to information from the Mexican Stock Exchange.
The company, created in mid 1996, was the result of a merger of Mexico's two largest airlines, Mexicana and Aeromexico. Both had previously traded separately.
A company spokesman told Reuters the figures only represented income at Cintra during the second half of the year, however.
If Cintra's second half net result was added to the first half results from Aeromexico and Mexicana, the total net profit for the year would have been 1.798 billion pesos, he said.
That compares to a combined loss for both airlines of 2.312 billion pesos during 1995, the company official said.

On a combined basis, the company's sales would have been 15.146 billion pesos versus 14.510 billion in 1995. Operating income would have been 1.602 billion pesos last year versus 693.6 million pesos in 1995.
For the second half of the year, Cintra's sales were 7.886 billion pesos, while its operating income was 914 million pesos.
